instructions.question: Which kind of work does `request.text` mainly ask the assistant to do?
instructions.focus: Judge what the user wants done, not which topics the text mentions.

new-feature.what: Build new behavior or a new capability in a project, such as a feature, module, endpoint, screen or integration spanning several files
new-feature.not_for: Plans, evaluations or decisions about how to build something without building it yet; restructuring that keeps behavior; fixing broken behavior

big-sweep.what: Apply one change across many places or domains, such as a migration, backfill, rename or upgrade across all modules, services or files
big-sweep.not_for: A change confined to one module or feature

bug.what: Investigate or fix something that is broken, failing, erroring or behaving unexpectedly

backend.what: Server-side application code: NestJS modules, controllers, services, API endpoints, queues or workers
backend.not_for: Database schema or migrations alone; LLM agent logic; Claude Code tooling or the EngineOS framework itself

frontend.what: Web user interface: React or Next.js components, pages, styling, client state or forms

mobile.what: React Native mobile app work: screens, navigation, native modules, or mirroring a web feature to mobile
mobile.not_for: Building, signing or publishing the app to an app store

ios-release.what: Build, sign or publish the iOS app to TestFlight or the Apple App Store

android-release.what: Build, sign or publish the Android app to Google Play
android-release.not_for: iOS or Apple App Store releases

llm.what: Build or change an LLM-powered product feature: a chatbot, prompts, retrieval, embeddings, model tool schemas, evals or Mastra agents inside an application
llm.not_for: Designing how several product agents coordinate; Claude Code subagents, hooks, skills or mods that help the developer work; the EngineOS framework's own agents

agent-system.what: Design the topology of a product system in which several AI agents cooperate: a supervisor, handoffs or orchestration between agents
agent-system.not_for: A single chatbot or agent; Claude Code development subagents

criteria.dba: Database layer work: SQL, schema design, migrations, indexes or query performance
criteria.devops: Infrastructure and delivery: CI/CD pipelines, GitHub workflows, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform or cloud resources
criteria.security-files: Change authentication, authorization, guards, middleware, secrets, credentials or environment-file handling

system-comprehension.what: Write documentation that explains how an existing system works, for onboarding or architecture understanding

criteria.interview-gaps: Have the assistant interview the user with questions to fill gaps in system documentation

qa-endpoints.what: Run end-to-end QA across all API endpoints of an integrated system, for example a Postman or Newman run
qa-endpoints.not_for: Writing unit or integration tests for specific code

audit.what: Run a read-only health check across a system or several domains to find what is broken or risky
audit.not_for: Reviewing one diff or pull request; writing onboarding documentation

criteria.refactor: Restructure or clean up existing code without changing its behavior: simplify, remove technical debt or rename

adr.what: Choose between technical options or decide how to structure something, and record the decision; includes planning or evaluating an architectural change before building it

criteria.release-notes: Write release notes or document what changed in a version

strategy.what: Business, market, career, positioning or monetization strategy

review.what: Review a diff, branch or pull request before merging, or judge whether a specific change is safe

criteria.test-writing: Write or add automated tests or test coverage for specific code
criteria.eval-setup: Set up evaluations or a golden set for an LLM feature
criteria.critic-verification: Independently challenge whether completed high-risk work is actually correct
criteria.handoff: Hand work over to another agent, wave or session with a written account of progress

retro.what: Run a retrospective over past work to propose improvements to rules, skills or registries

task-observer.what: Log one observation about friction with a rule or skill noticed during work

record-change.what: Write or close the change record that describes work already done
record-change.not_for: Confirming that the work is correct

verify-done.what: Confirm that work is done, shipped or ready to archive, with evidence

criteria.route-planning: Ask which agents should handle a request or how to split it into a dispatch plan

other.what: None of the listed kinds of work: a general question, or work outside these categories, such as configuring Claude Code itself (hooks, settings, mods or the status line)
other.not_for: Requests that fit one of the listed kinds of work

work.what: Build new behavior or a new capability in a project, such as a feature, module, endpoint, screen or integration spanning several files
work.not_for: Plans, evaluations or decisions about how to build something without building it yet; restructuring that keeps behavior; fixing broken behavior

is_project_change.instructions: Does `request.text` ask the assistant to change files in a project, such as code, configuration, documentation or design files?

criteria.true: Asks for something to be built, edited, written or removed in the project
criteria.false: Only asks for an explanation, an answer, an opinion or advice

design_work.instructions: Does `request.text` ask for design work, such as an architecture, an interface or contract, a data model or a plan, before implementation?

fact.large_change.instructions: Does `request.text` ask to rewrite, overhaul or re-architect a large part of a system?

fact.affects_public_contract.instructions: Would the work in `request.text` change a public or published API, a database schema, an event payload or another contract that external consumers depend on?

fact.handles_sensitive_data.instructions: Does the work in `request.text` involve personal data, payment data, health data, credentials, or data protected by privacy law such as LGPD or GDPR?

fact.production_write.instructions: Does `request.text` ask for an action that directly changes a production environment, such as deploying, releasing or writing to live systems?

fact.destructive_ddl_or_dml.instructions: Does the work in `request.text` involve deleting data or dropping or truncating database tables, columns, indexes or schemas?

fact.secret_reached_git_or_shared_file.instructions: Does `request.text` report that a secret, API key, token, password or credential was committed, pushed, leaked or exposed?

fact.knowledge_changes_frequently.instructions: Does the work in `request.text` involve retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings or fine-tuning?

fact.multi_agent_system.instructions: Does `request.text` ask to design or build a product system in which more than one AI agent cooperates?

criteria.true: A product with several cooperating agents, such as a supervisor with workers or agents handing off to each other
criteria.false: A single agent or chatbot, or Claude Code subagents that the developer uses while working

fact.retrieval_over_shared_corpus.instructions: Does the work in `request.text` involve retrieving documents from a corpus shared by several users or tenants?

scale.instructions: How widely does the work in `request.text` spread across the project?
criteria: A single focused change or question in one place
Several related changes within one area or domain
Changes spanning several domains, or the same change repeated across many modules, services or files

risk.reversibility.instructions: If the work in `request.text` is carried out, how hard is it to undo?
criteria: Trivially undone, for example by reverting a commit
Can be undone, but only with real effort
Irreversible, or reversible only with data loss

risk.blast_radius.instructions: If the work in `request.text` is carried out, how far do its effects reach?
criteria: Confined to one module and the local machine
Affects a whole service or one team's surface
Reaches production, other teams or external consumers

risk.data_sensitivity.instructions: What kind of data does the work in `request.text` touch?
criteria: Personal, credential, financial or clinical data

risk.contract_surface.instructions: Which interfaces does the work in `request.text` change?
criteria: A public or published API, a database schema or an event payload

risk.spend.instructions: What money does the work in `request.text` commit?
criteria: An unbounded cost, or a commitment of real money
